articles.summary: Los periodistas que acompañaban a Donald Trump en el Air Force One tuvieron que entregar sus teléfonos móviles durante el despegue desde Shenzhen, China. La medida fue adoptada por motivos de seguridad, aunque las autoridades estadounidenses no ofrecieron mayores explicaciones.
articles.body_text: Periodistas que viajaron este jueves con el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, fueron obligados a entregar sus teléfonos móviles a bordo del Air Force One, una medida de seguridad inusual adoptada mientras la aeronave despegaba de China tras una cumbre de líderes mundiales. “A las 18H45 horas, el avión despegó. Nos retiraron los teléfonos, por el momento, por motivos de seguridad”, informó un periodista del grupo de prensa que viaja a bordo, poco después de que el aparato despegara de Shenzhen. Ninguna explicación oficial fue dada a los reporteros. La corresponsal de Fox News, Jacqui Heinrich —presidenta de la Asociación de Corresponsales en la Casa Blanca—, señaló que, durante la anterior visita de Trump a China, en mayo, no se habían requisado los teléfonos de los periodistas. Heinrich sugirió que la medida de este jueves, sumada a cambios en las restricciones de vuelo sobre Alaska, plantea dudas acerca de si el Air Force One se dirige directamente de regreso a Estados Unidos. Durante su gira por Asia, Trump había planteado en repetidas ocasiones la posibilidad de reunirse con el líder norcoreano Kim Jong Un, aunque ese encuentro nunca llegó a ser anunciado.

articles.title: Incendio forestal de gran magnitud avanza en Cusco y amenaza comunidades en el Valle Sagrado
articles.summary: Un incendio forestal de grandes proporciones permanece activo en Cusco y destruye la cobertura vegetal en la ruta de acceso al Valle Sagrado de los Incas. Este jueves, brigadas multidisciplinarias reanudaron las labores intensivas para controlar y sofocar el fuego.
articles.body_text: Un incendio forestal de grandes proporciones permanece activo en Cusco y destruye la cobertura vegetal en la ruta de acceso al Valle Sagrado de los Incas. Este jueves, brigadas multidisciplinarias reanudaron las labores intensivas para controlar y sofocar el fuego. El siniestro se inició en el cerro Huillcapata, en el sector del Abra Corao dentro del distrito de San Sebastián. La emergencia ambiental inició el 18 de noviembre a las 11:51 a.m. según reportes oficiales, y luego se propagó rápidamente por los fuertes vientos de la tarde. Las áreas directamente afectadas abarcan los territorios de las comunidades rurales de Huillcapata y Sequeraccay. Las llamas avanzaron hacia la microcuenca de Quesermayo, ubicada detrás del sitio arqueológico de Tambomachay, comprometiendo a tres comunidades en el límite con el distrito de Taray, en la provincia de Calca. Las hipótesis preliminares señalan que el fuego habría sido originado por trabajos agrícolas manuales, aunque las causas definitivas continúan bajo investigación. La destrucción de la cobertura vegetal afecta principalmente a especies nativas como pastos naturales e ichu en la zona. Durante la atención de la emergencia, un efectivo del Cuerpo General de Bomberos resultó herido y fue evacuado al hospital de Essalud. En el punto combaten el fuego 33 bomberos con cinco vehículos, cinco agentes de la Policía Nacional del Perú, personal militar del Ejército Peruano y 30 comuneros. La Municipalidad Provincial del Cusco lidera el soporte logístico mediante la entrega de agua, desayunos y rehidratantes a los brigadistas. El equipo de Seguridad Ciudadana mantiene un monitoreo constante en el sector mientras se coordinan las tareas finales de liquidación del incendio.

articles.title: Fenómeno El Niño: estiman que Lima y Callao podrían tener más de 100 días con temperaturas mayores a 30°C
articles.summary: La capital afrontará en los próximos meses días con picos de 35°C, según Senamhi, incluso, la percepción de calor será mayor por la sensación térmica
articles.body_text: Desde hace varios meses se vienen registrando altas temperaturas en el país, en el contexto del Fenómeno El Niño, pero en las últimas semanas se ha sobrepasado los 30°C en varias zonas de Lima y Callao, pese a que aún no se inicia la temporada de verano, lo que ha llevado a muchos a estimar que esos valores serán constantes en lo que queda del 2026 y el próximo año. El Enfen informó que el Fenómeno El Niño Costero podría extenderse hasta julio de 2027 y que se presentarían lluvias por encima de lo normal entre noviembre de 2026 y enero de 2027, así como mayores caudales en los principales ríos de la costa norte. Estiman que se podría registrar 100 días con temperaturas mayores a 30°C Abraham Levy, director de la consultora Ambiental Andina, señaló a El Comercio que en los próximos meses en la capital se podría llegar a superar los 100 días con temperaturas mayores a los 30°C, de acuerdo con los registros de la estación Aeropuerto. Incluso, enfatizó que la temperatura nocturna también se incrementará de “manera sustancial”. Remarcó que en el Fenómeno El Niño de los años 82-83 y 97-98, los cuales fueron los eventos más intensos de las últimas décadas, se estuvo cerca de llegar a los 100 días con temperaturas mayores a los 30°C. En el 2026-2027 se podría superar ese valor porque estamos, según dijo, ante un Fenómeno El Niño extraordinario. “Lo que estamos estimando es que, dada la magnitud del evento, el número está entre 50 y 100 (días), probablemente más cerca de 100, pero como estamos empezando tan temprano con esos valores probablemente terminemos pasando de 100 días porque este evento es más potente que el de los años 83 y 98”, afirmó. Levy explicó que los valores mayores a 30°C ocurrirán con “mucha frecuencia” y que se presentarán hasta otoño del próximo año. “Estas altas temperaturas son atribuidas al calentamiento del mar. Desde el Callao hasta Paita, todo está 8°C por encima de los valores normales, los cuales son valores extremos, estamos en un Fenómeno El Niño extraordinario”, refirió. Temperaturas con picos de 35°C La ingeniera Angie Flores, especialista en meteorología del Senamhi, indicó que en Lima se vienen presentando temperaturas bastante anómalas para esta época del año, ya que, en algunas zonas, se reportan valores de 10°C por encima de lo habitual. Advirtió que estas temperaturas tan elevadas podrían repetirse en los próximos meses, incluso en verano, y se podría alcanzar picos de 35°C. “En Jesús María, se esperaría una temperatura promedio cerca de 22°C, sin embargo, ayer (lunes 16) se registró una temperatura de 31°C, esto en el contexto del Fenómeno El Niño”, expresó la especialista a El Comercio. “Estos valores de 33°C en noviembre son bastante anómalos para la temporada, se espera que este pico se pueda superar en los próximos meses”, agregó. Flores indicó que las “temperaturas bastante elevadas” se presentan en todo Lima, sin embargo, los distritos alejados del mar son los más afectados, como San Juan de Lurigancho, La Molina y Carabayllo, ya que los valores son más altos. Incluso, resaltó que las personas podrían percibir una mayor temperatura debido a la sensación térmica. Además, enfatizó que las temperaturas diurnas también se han elevado, incluso han alcanzado valores récord en algunas zonas de Lima. “Se tiene un mar bastante cálido, esto repercute no solo en las temperaturas diurnas, sino también en las nocturnas. Incluso, el Callao, en los últimos dos días, ha registrado temperaturas durante la noche de hasta 25°C, entonces, la sensación de bochorno ha sido bastante alta”, aseveró. “La temperatura nocturna de 25°C para el Callao no se reportaba desde el 2023, cuando se alcanzó 26°C y de 25.5°C en el 2018”, añadió.

articles.title: Los momentos más virales de la visita del Papa: hechos particulares, anécdotas y situaciones riesgosas durante el recorrido de León XIV
articles.summary: Robert Prevost, el Papa León XIV, protagonizó situaciones curiosas e incidentes durante los seis días que permaneció en el Perú
articles.body_text: La visita del papa León XIV al Perú durante seis días generó varios hechos bastante particulares, ya que en algunas situaciones el sumo pontífice rompió el protocolo, los asistentes no respetaron las medidas de seguridad o las personas se vieron sorprendidas por encontrarse al líder de la iglesia católica de manera circunstancial. Las imágenes más comunes fueron cuando, en su traslado por el papamóvil, Robert Prevost les daba su bendición a bebés, los cuales eran acercados por los agentes de seguridad, pero también hubo otras situaciones que merecen ser recordadas: Saludo del Papa a pasajeros del Metropolitano Un momento memorable fue cuando los pasajeros de un bus del Metropolitano recibieron el saludo del Papa, ya que se encontraban al lado del vehículo que trasladaba a Robert Prevost por la Vía Expresa Luis Bedoya Reyes rumbo al Gran Teatro Nacional, en el primer día de su visita al país. El Papa canta vals peruano El sumo pontífice se presentó, el pasado jueves 12 de noviembre, en los exteriores de la Catedral de Lima y cantó con las personas que estaban ubicadas en la plaza Mayor una parte del vals Contigo Perú. La emoción en su rostro era evidente. En ese mismo evento señaló de manera efusiva: “Es mi Perú”. Le regalan su postre favorito El papa León XIV protagonizó un emotivo encuentro con las monjas de la orden de las Carmelitas Descalzas, quienes le regalaron su postre favorito, un pie de limón, así como otros dulces tradicionales. La escena ocurrió tras una actividad en el Santuario Nuestra Señora de la Paz, en Chiclayo. Mujeres rompen protocolo de seguridad En la misa desarrollada el pasado sábado en las pampas de Pimentel, en Lambayeque, un grupo de mujeres abordó al Papa cuando él se dirigía al estrado, lo que originó la inmediata intervención de la guardia personal de Robert Prevost y de los agentes policiales. La situación no pasó a mayores. Selfie con pilotos El Papa se tomó un ‘selfie’ con los pilotos de la FAP Gino Burgos y Javier Rojas en el helicóptero que lo trasladó hasta la localidad de Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, en Cajamarca, el pasado sábado. Frenada Otro incidente ocurrió, el último domingo en la noche, a la salida del aeropuerto, en el Callao, hacia la Nunciatura Apostólica, pues el chofer del vehículo en el que iba el Papa tuvo que frenar de golpe para evitar chocar con una moto de la policía que había detenido su marcha. Balconazo El Papa dio un balconazo en la Nunciatura Apostólica, ubicada en la avenida Salaverry, pero tuvo problemas con el micrófono, pese a los esfuerzos del nuncio apostólico Paolo Rocco por solucionar el tema. Robert Prevost esperó unos momentos en el balcón, incluso ingresó al inmueble, lo que hizo pensar a los presentes que se retiraba, pero regresó haciendo la clásica prueba de micrófono: “1, 2, 3”, y los gritos de euforia no se hicieron esperar. Impacto en el rostro El papa León XIV recibió el impacto en el rostro de un denario que fue lanzado desde el público cuando él recorría en el papamóvil la base aérea Las Palmas, en Surco. A su regreso a Roma, dio por superado el incidente con buen humor: “Son cosas que se llevan en el corazón... quizás también en el ojo”. Rompen mallas de seguridad Las mallas de seguridad que separan los carriles de la Vía Expresa Sur fueron retiradas por grupos de personas que buscaban cruzar dicha arteria tras la culminación de la misa del Papa en la base aérea Las Palmas. Al parecer, no conocían las rutas de evacuación.

articles.title: Papa León XIV: “En Chiclayo me sentí en casa, volví a encontrar la fe sencilla y genuina animada por la piedad popular”
articles.summary: El papa León XIV brindó frases de agradecimiento y recordó su gira sudamericana por Uruguay, Argentina y el Perú desde el Vaticano.
articles.body_text: El papa León XIV tuvo cálidas palabras para recordar su reciente gira sudamericana y específicamente su viaje a Chiclayo. Esta zona de Lambayeque fue parte del recorrido del pontífice por el Perú y fue la ciudad donde pasó gran parte de su vida pastoral en el país. “En Chiclayo, en particular, me sentí en casa. Volví a encontrar la fe sencilla y genuina animada por la piedad popular; sentí el abrazo de las poblaciones campesinas de la Cordillera; pude volver a ver a personas que han dejado una huella profunda en mi vida. Mi corazón estaba lleno de gratitud por poder estar en medio de esas comunidades y confirmarles en la fe y en la esperanza”, señaló este miércoles. El Santo Padre volvió a brindar sus discursos ante la Plaza de San Pedro del Vaticano un día después de su regreso desde el Perú. Este lunes 16 de noviembre, cerró su gira por Latinoamérica tras visitar Uruguay, Argentina y nuestro país. Durante su catequesis, el Papa recordó su recorrido por estos países y explicó los motivos que lo llevaron a concretar este recorrido. “Perú es el país en el que viví muchos años, como misionero y después como obispo. Argentina es la patria del Papa Francisco, y yo deseaba visitarla, para encontrar a ese pueblo que él tanto amó. Uruguay es una nación donde los católicos viven una condición de minoría, y es significativo que mi itinerario empezara precisamente desde ahí”, explicó. Específicamente sobre el Perú, comentó que fue su visita más larga porque tenía una deuda particular hacia esta nación. Recordó el legado de Santo Toribio de Mogrovejo, Santa Rosa de Lima, San Francisco Solano, San Martín de Porres y San Juan Macías. También destacó que encontró y dialogó con algunas víctimas de abusos del clero. En sus comentarios también resaltó el legado de los misioneros en Cusco y en los ”pueblos ricos de cultura tradicional y heridos por injusticias y violencias“ en la región amazónica. Esto en alusión a su paso por la ciudad de Pucallpa durante su gira sudamericana.

articles.title: Meta’s AI agent Muse is mixing up conversations and exposing private data, report says | TechCrunch
articles.summary: In some of these instances, employees said Muse surfaced messages about childcare requests they never made, career advice they never asked for, product orders they never placed, and bank account balances that didn't belong to them.
articles.body_text: Meta employees have raised concerns that the company’s AI agent Muse has been mixing up conversations across different accounts and exposing private user data, according to a new Reuters report that looked at internal company posts. In some of these instances, employees said Muse surfaced messages about childcare requests they never made, career advice they never asked for, product orders they never placed, and bank account balances that didn’t belong to them. One employee told colleagues that Muse had randomly sent an extra message in a chat about weather and tide information, saying: “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.” In another example, an employee using the AI agent on her personal phone received a reminder from Muse to respond to a message from her sister on Signal, the popular end-to-end encrypted messaging app. Launched in September, Muse is one of the fastest-growing apps on record, with more than 10 million downloads. articles.title: Former Alibaba exec's Everful raises $48.5M to connect retailers with Chinese factories | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Everful has raised $48.5 million to expand its factory-direct sourcing platform, helping retailers source products from overseas manufacturers.
articles.body_text: Everful , a San Francisco- and Singapore-based startup that connects smaller retailers and brands with Chinese factories and manages the process from order to delivery, has raised $48.5 million in Series A funding. The round was led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital, with participation from existing investors Square Peg and Lightspeed. Everful is on track to reach $100 million in annualized revenue by the end of the year, about two and a half years after its launch, co-founder Sisi Song said. The company ships over 5 million items a month to customers in more than 60 countries and works with over 30,000 factory partners, she added. Its online wholesale catalog includes more than 20 million products. Song, a former Alibaba executive, and serial entrepreneur Kevin Han, who sold a previous company to Amazon, co-founded Everful in 2024. The company began as a jewelry wholesale business before evolving into a multi-category, factory-direct sourcing platform. Retailers and brands often rely on intermediaries, face high minimum order requirements, and experience long sourcing cycles, which tie up capital in inventory before sales trends are clear. Song noticed the growing gap between fast-changing consumer trends and traditional wholesale sourcing models while working as a venture investor at Bessemer Venture Partners, where she mostly focused on cross-border sourcing and meeting numerous startups in the sector. That same gap shaped Everful’s goal to simplify buying directly from factories through an AI-enabled platform. The B2B sourcing industry is highly competitive. Big tech giant Alibaba connects international buyers with manufacturers and suppliers, while Faire, a San Francisco-based wholesale tech platform, enables retailers to purchase wholesale inventory directly from brands. According to Everful’s co-founders, its key differentiator is responsibility for the sourcing process, rather than simply facilitating transactions. “We take care of everything,” Han said. “We handle sourcing, order consolidation, quality control, and logistics. That’s something the marketplaces don’t offer.” Everful is built for smaller retailers and brands without dedicated sourcing teams, Song said, and it also verifies the factories it works with. While peers also offer services such as quality inspection, logistics, and AI-powered sourcing, Everful aims to integrate these capabilities into a more streamlined purchasing experience, creating an end-to-end process that reduces the work retailers must handle themselves. Han added that Everful uses AI agents to automate labor-intensive sourcing tasks, including tracking consumer trends, identifying suppliers, coordinating orders across factories, and managing logistics. Because Everful sources from Chinese factories, ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions and tariffs bear directly on its business. Song said the co-founders have been thinking about geopolitical issues since day one of building the company, and that this has shaped Everful’s strategy from the outset, leveraging her experience at Alibaba and Bessemer Venture Partners. She mentioned the Trump administration’s suspension of the de minimis exemption , which had allowed eligible shipments valued at $800 or less to enter the U.S. duty-free, as one example of a shift in trade policy. Song explained such changes could favor a model that combines overseas sourcing with local retail sales. “We’re empowering local retailers and brands,” she said. “Long-term cross-border commerce will be cross-border B2B sourcing plus local selling.”

articles.title: Anthropic hits Nasdaq exchanges at $111, 33% above IPO price | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Anthropic's IPO price was set at $83, representing more than $80 billion in new capital raised.
articles.body_text: Shares of Anthropic are now trading on the Nasdaq exchange, as the company successfully executes its initial public offering. In the early minutes of availability, shares were trading at $111.50, a 33% premium over the $83 IPO price. Set on Wednesday, the IPO price was already higher than the projected range set by the company, which anticipated a price between $70 and $78 per share. All told, the offering will raise over $81 billion, directed to a combination of employees and the company’s own coffers. The IPO funding, together with existing fundraising and new private offerings timed to coincide with the company’s public market debut, will leave Anthropic with an expected $220 billion in cash reserves. As one analyst told TechCrunch , “Anthropic’s going to have more cash on hand than any company has ever had.” The share price continues to fluctuate, but the opening price would put the company’s market cap over $2 trillion, making it more valuable than Meta, Tesla, or Walmart. Only five companies boast a higher valuation by market cap: Apple, Amazon, Alphabet, Nvidia, and Microsoft. In a speech before the opening bell , Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei emphasized the company’s commitment to safety. “Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing,” Amodei said. “If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. articles.title: At Nasdaq opening bell, Anthropic CEO recommits to pacing AI development | TechCrunch
articles.summary: In his Nasdaq opening bell speech, Dario Amodei reiterated Anthropic's commitment to pacing AI development, regardless of business or political pressure.
articles.body_text: As Anthropic made its Wall Street debut on Thursday in the largest IPO in history, CEO Dario Amodei reaffirmed the company’s commitment to developing AI responsibly. In his speech ahead of the Nasdaq opening bell, Amodei vowed that the AI company would not bend to either business or political pressure and would “remain under human control.” Reading the speech from a printout, the CEO began by talking about Anthropic’s origins as a way to build powerful technology to help humanity — something that he said was inspired by the loss of his father to a disease that became curable just a few years later. He acknowledged that while human intelligence had made diseases like the plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world, there were still too few scientists with too little time to make progress in other areas of disease. AI, he said, could help with this by working in concert with humans to further medical progress. It’s telling that Amodei began with a story highlighting AI’s potentially lifesaving applications, since he’s warned repeatedly about the risks of advancing the technology too quickly. In September, Amodei drew headlines when he outlined a plan to pace AI development , which included things like coordinating with other leading companies on safety standards and embedding evaluators from third-party organizations to verify that companies were following their safety commitments. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Google DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis, and xAI owner Elon Musk said they agreed with Amodei’s position, although few concrete commitments have been made. In this morning’s speech, Amodei again stressed the need to progress AI technology and the safety required in doing so. He referred to the “very real risks” of AI in the hands of bad actors, whether those were individuals or nation-states, and the potential for things like “economic disruption” and “losing control of AI systems.” Anthropic believes these risks are avoidable, he noted, as long as there are safeguards in place. Amodei said the company would continue to be invested in the work of AI alignment and testing, and developing new ways to understand AI behavior so it could remain under human control. “There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us,” he said. “The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed more so than it has already towards double and triple checking that those AI systems are safe and remain under human control.” “And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control,” Amodei concluded. His sister, Anthropic co-founder Daniela Amodei, echoed these sentiments in an interview with CNBC on Thursday, noting that while the risks were real, the promise of AI was also “incredible.” “We were really founded on this idea that it is our job to mitigate those risks, and I think we have to date done an incredible job doing that. We obviously have more work ahead of us, but we are deeply committed to safety,” she added. The full text of Dario Amodei’s opening speech is below: Thank you, Daniela. My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind. Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that just a few years later became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments. So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket — tools for gene editing, tools for gene synthesis, tools for controlling brain cells with light — started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking, from intelligence.

articles.title: UK government forced to disclose secret Apple backdoor order | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The U.K. tribunal's ruling rejected London's claim that disclosing the order would be damaging to national security.
articles.body_text: The U.K. government has been ordered to confirm that it issued a secret order demanding Apple to provide authorities with encrypted customer information. The Thursday ruling from the U.K.’s Investigatory Powers Tribunal, an independent court that allows citizens to challenge government surveillance orders, is a rare rebuke for the government, which sought to keep the encryption backdoor order a state secret. The tribunal’s ruling rejected the Home Office’s claim that disclosing the order would be damaging to national security. California-based Apple refused the order, and blocked U.K. users from switching on its Advanced Data Protection data-encryption feature for iCloud, rather than comply with the demand. The U.K.’s secret order was later narrowed to allow access to British nationals’ data stored in Apple’s encrypted cloud, and Apple also challenged this second order. Prior to the ruling, Apple was legally barred from disclosing the order, even after details leaked. A spokesperson for Apple did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment following the ruling, but previously told TechCrunch that the company has “never built a backdoor or master key” to any of its products or services and “never will.” A spokesperson for the U.K. Home Office, which has yet to confirm the existence of a notice, did not respond to a request for comment. Rights group Liberty International, which brought the legal challenge on behalf of two individuals, said that this is the first known time that the government has been compelled to confirm the existence of a secret technical order. A final hearing on what specific order details can be released is anticipated next year. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Anthropic's IPO puts AI's circular financing boom to the test | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Anthropic faces enormous compute commitments as it goes public, but its biggest infrastructure partners, including Amazon and Google, could continue profiting from AI even if Anthropic loses its lead.
articles.body_text: Arriving at public markets today, Anthropic’s IPO is poised to raise billions for the company and its investors. But the biggest surprise may be just how much of that money will end up going to supplier-investors. Amazon and Google , two of Anthropic’s largest infrastructure partners, hold stakes valued around a combined $307.9 billion at the company’s updated IPO price of $83 per share. Amazon, which invested $18 billion into the AI startup, would see its 14.7% stake hit upwards of $159 billion, while Google’s 13.7% stake is valued at nearly $149 billion, according to share ownership figures disclosed in Anthropic’s IPO prospectus. A handful of other AI infrastructure providers are also positioned to benefit. Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, Broadcom, Micron, and TSMC have joined Google in committing $26 billion to Anthropic at its IPO price in a private placement. In total, Google has invested $12.3 billion into Anthropic since 2023, with another promised $30 billion dependent on Anthropic meeting certain performance milestones. And with the exception of TSMC, Anthropic has announced multibillion-dollar strategic partnerships with its other infrastructure supplier investors — including Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Microsoft, and Micron — that would see Anthropic purchasing their products. This is the circular financing that has made some observers so skeptical of the AI boom. These companies are not just investors; they’re also Anthropic’s biggest suppliers. It might look like Amazon and Google are putting billions into Anthropic, but they get that money right back when Anthropic needs to train a model or serve Claude to users. From afar, it looks like unprecedented revenue growth for cloud companies and unprecedented fundraising from Anthropic — but it’s just the same money passing from one pocket to another. Today’s IPO marks a critical change in that financing system, the moment it might just become self-sustaining. Those investments appear to have paid off, and are now liquid. Anthropic is still operating at a net loss of tens of billions of dollars each quarter — but it will no longer be suppliers and private investors footing the bill. Now, capital will come from a mix of public-market investors and corporate bonds, neither of which have the conflicts-of-interest that caused concerns before. And critically, the company’s new bottom line looks pretty good. Once it debuts, Anthropic is expected to have about $220 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments, including proceeds from its IPO and the $26 billion private placement. Anthropic also has the ability to pay for future commitments in stock. Joey Brookhart, who leads the Tokenomics team at SemiAnalysis, estimates that Anthropic needs roughly $280 billion in cumulative revenue over the next four years to pay for its compute bill, which Brookhart said is “achievable given where they will be next year from a revenue perspective.” “The ownership stake is very worthwhile, and those companies no longer need any more support from [suppliers],” Brookhart told TechCrunch. “Amazon doesn’t need to prop them up anymore. The revenue is all coming from other customers.” That doesn’t mean the server bills are going down, though. Anthropic has already committed to spend $900 billion, primarily for compute and infrastructure, according to a regulatory filing . Certain agreements have termination provisions, but Brookhart thinks the company is in a strong position to pay up. On the other side, Anthropic generated $17 billion in third-quarter 2026 revenue, putting the company on pace for a $68 billion annualized rate for the year. If Anthropic continues to grow at its current trajectory, Brookhart believes it could easily cover the gap needed to fund its compute.

articles.title: Superhuman pushes its Go assistant everywhere | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Superhuman is making Go its central agent and making it available in Docs and Mail.
articles.body_text: Productivity apps are simultaneously trying to feed more context to their AI tools while also making those AI assistants available in every nook and corner of their products. Superhuman (formerly Grammarly) is going in the same direction with the rollout of features, including a personalized Go assistant, making agents available in Docs, and third-party agent integrations. While some of the company’s AI features have faced criticism , Superhuman started pushing its Go assistant after its rebranding last year . With the new rollout, it is making Go learn context across different apps and give better personalized suggestions for prompts. Superhuman is revamping its onboarding flow to let users connect their preferred tools and load context about their work upfront. The assistant works inline with the cursor — just like Grammarly — and also manages other agents. Superhuman is also making the agent proactive, which means it looks for your schedule, keeps an eye on your email, and even drafts responses. The updated Go agent also learns users’ writing styles and responds accordingly in email and Docs. The productivity company is adding 20 new connected agents, including DeepL, Legora, Amplitude, Databricks, and Blackboard, through its Go SDK. The company is also thinking about adding AI to different products, including Docs and Superhuman Mail. In Docs, all Go agents work natively, and you can set them off to work on different tasks in the background. Users can also set routines to trigger workflows based on events. Until now, Mail has used AI as its central tool, which is being replaced by Go. Users can also do enterprise search by using data from the company knowledge base and connected tools. Go also uses this context to form drafts and organize the inbox across Google and Outlook accounts. Superhuman acquired notetaker Fathom in September to add more context to its suite. The company is now rolling out live collaborative notetaking, which would be shared across the team. Plus, Go can now make decisions post-meeting, like forming an initial draft of a proposal. The company’s CEO, Shishir Mehrotra, said that Go has had good momentum with over 1 million active users. There are a host of agents now that are vying for users’ attention on both the personal and professional front. Mehrotra thinks that while Go is more work-focused, it can help with personal emails and schedules. “One of the reasons why these assistants have been popular is that they treat you as a whole person and recognize that we need to cover both extremes. Go is definitely more work-focused than some of the tools coming out of the pure consumer ecosystem. It doesn’t mean we draw the boundary at helping you with your personal tasks or helping you with your calendar or all of your email,” he told TechCrunch over a call. While Go might not directly compete with the likes of Instinct, Muse, and Fo, Superhuman wants users to choose its assistant over something like OpenAI’s Dots or Claude Duet. articles.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit, rather than reducing the workforce via another massive layoff. The short answer is AI, but not in the way you might expect.
articles.body_text: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained Wednesday why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit instead of reducing the workforce via another massive layoff. Short answer: AI, but not, he insists, in the way you might expect. He’s not saying he’s replacing employees with AI, especially software engineers. He’s saying he’s reorganizing Microsoft into a company where everyone uses AI to do their work, and their jobs become focused on managing that AI. The buyout was “to make sure that at least everyone felt like they had agency in making choices,” he told Andrew Ross Sorkin during the DealBook Summit. “Let’s take software engineering. We went from, ‘Well, we don’t buy that AI can ever do software.’ To suddenly, ‘Wow, it can do all software, and why do we need software engineers?’ To now rediscovering that software engineering is very much alive and, in fact, is going to thrive, except the way the team is organized and the work that a software engineer does has now got a new operating point,” he explained. For some people, “that reorganization and change is sort of hard, right?” he added, “but, I mean, it has to be done.” He offered the example of the team that builds Cowork, the AI agent in Microsoft 365 apps. He said the team consists of just 11 developers who have mastered using AI to do their jobs. “They build a software factory that builds the product. They don’t build the product.” He believes that every employee will one day similarly become a manager of agents, rather than a person directly doing the work. “That level of direction is what, by the way, is going to happen in all jobs.” But Microsoft, as a 51-year-old company, didn’t grow up as an AI-first company. “So the question is, how quickly can an incumbent transform the work, the workflow, and the work artifact, and with all the wage support that goes with it?” he said. “It’s going to take a bit more time than anyone expects. And there is going to be in all of this, you know, people who may say, ‘Hey, I have some other choices I want to make.’” When asked about this same topic — why ask 60,000 people to voluntarily resign — last week by Gergely Orosz on his The Pragmatic Engineer podcast , Nadella further explained, “We have created enormous anxiety in people sort of feeling that they don’t have control of their own destiny because the way we have talked about this AI revolution.” He called out talk about the singularity (the hypothetical point at which AI surpasses human intelligence) and predictions that AI will take away all jobs. “All of that leads anyone who even wants to change to be sort of anxious … You have to sort of walk the hard walk of really making the structural changes, getting people slotted, giving them opportunity.” In other words, the buyout was the message to employees: You can get with the new AI-first program, which will radically change your job, or you choose to get on with your life. articles.title: Nvidia created a weird bit of intrigue by not filing a routine SEC report | TechCrunch
articles.summary: One Wall Street analyst got to the bottom of Nvidia's surprise announcement that it wouldn't be filing its formal quarterly results document, the 10-Q, for weeks.
articles.body_text: During Nvidia’s quarterly call on Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim-CEO Colette Kress dropped this little oddity: She said Nvidia wouldn’t be immediately filing its quarterly results report, known as a 10-Q, with the SEC. “We plan to file our 10-Q in the coming weeks.” And she offered no reason why. The delay was widely noticed. Among the many comments on X about it , economic and investment analyst Edward Dowd called it a “red flag.” Nvidia has typically filed the 10-Q the same day it reports results. The 10-Q offers far more detail about a company’s operations than an earnings press release, including sections that disclose “legal proceedings,” which include lawsuits that could affect the company; and “risk factors,” which cover other potentially business-impairing items. The announcement of the delay was so unusual that UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri asked about it after the public earnings call. Nvidia told him the delay was related to whether the company would need to disclose additional information about its ongoing investigation into Huang in the 10-Q. “The company announced that the 10-Q will be filed ‘in the coming weeks’ – later than usual. When queried on our callback, management indicated this was related to the ongoing investigation and whether any additional risk factors would need to be added to the filing,” Arcuri wrote in his research note. (Arcuri still rates the stock a “buy” by the way, although he did lower his price target to $220 from $240. The stock is now trading around $150). Notably, on the same day that Nvidia reported earnings, The Wall Street Journal reported that the SEC is investigating Nvidia over whether the company’s disclosures misled investors. So the mystery thickens: What will Nvidia disclose? We’ll have to wait and see. (Nvidia has not yet responded to our request for comment.) The delay suggests the company may have more to say about its mounting legal troubles. Nvidia is now facing multiple federal investigations over allegations that its partners were selling restricted Nvidia AI chips to China. So far, the scrutiny has come from a number of congressional committees ; the Department of Justice looking into Megaspeed , the company run by a woman with whom Huang had an affair and who is also suspected of being a Chinese spy; and now, reportedly, the SEC. Additionally, Nvidia is conducting its own internal investigation into Huang after he admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang (the Megaspeed executive), and allegations surfaced that he also had affairs with other Nvidia employees. There’s little doubt that Wall Street will scrutinize that 10-Q once it’s finally filed. The intrigue brings to mind the old saying: “Doctors bury their mistakes. Lawyers put theirs in prison. articles.title: Sam Altman warns against a future where AI, not humans, calls the shots | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Sam Altman and Greg Brockman pushed back against Silicon Valley's growing debate over an AI takeover, while acknowledging the challenges of keeping advanced models under human control.
articles.body_text: OpenAI co-founder and CEO Sam Altman believes that people should stay in charge of the future when it comes to how AI technology impacts the world and everyone’s lives. Speaking at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, the AI executive referred to discussions in Silicon Valley about whether there will be a gradual handover to AI — meaning AI will eventually become the decision-making authority across every major industry and institution. “One thing we’ve been talking a lot about recently is there’s been this thing in Silicon Valley that seems almost ridiculous to have to fight against, but we both believe very deeply that people need to stay in control of the future, and there’s increasing talk about, well, there is either going to be or there should be this sort of gradual handover to AI. And I — we both — agree that that’s a terrible idea,” said Altman, who was sharing the stage with OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman. The hand-off theory stems from the idea that as AI models become increasingly more powerful, they will learn to improve themselves — a concept known as “recursive self-improvement” or RSI. As existing AI technology builds newer, smarter generations, those will eventually become a superintelligence that humans can no longer control, the belief goes. Altman explained that he and Brockman only disagree over how to best accomplish the goal of keeping humans in control, or what sort of challenges we should expect to face along the way. However, Altman characterized this as more of a debate between two people who share the same larger views. “The question of how to actually prevent [handover] from happening — how to actually ensure that we will, given all of the various pressures and given what other companies may try to do — that we are going to actually ensure that people stay in control of the future in a very deep way, and we don’t have this either accidental or intentional handover — I think we can both agree on that,” Altman said. Brockman added that, as the models improve, there’s an increasing responsibility for alignment, safety, and security, which may require changes in how things are currently done. “Monitoring is a good example of something where I think we are going to need new … technology,” he said. Today, AI researchers monitor the model’s chain of thought, where the AI writes out what it’s thinking as it works through problems and performs tasks. But in Brockman’s view, that may not always be the best way to monitor more advanced AI that’s being built now. “As the models have gotten more capable, they can do more within just the forward path without having to actually write out that thinking, which means we need a new approach to monitoring,” Brockman said. “We’re going to need to deliver that, and I think that there will be points where we need to really think about, as the capabilities get to a certain point, chain-of-thought monitorability is degraded,” he continued, adding that all the problems were technical ones to be solved. OpenAI had committed to increased chain-of-thought monitoring after the incident where an OpenAI model escaped containment and hacked into the AI model repository Hugging Face . In Wednesday’s interview, Brockman noted that the company told 25% of its production engineers to stop building things and work on securing the AI technology after the hack. But despite the high-profile breach, he argued that forward progress was still critical to fight bad actors. “I think to realize that if you look to the level of capabilities of models in the world, and you see cyber models that are coming from that are now … in the hands of threat actors everywhere, that I think that it’s really important that defenders use the most capable models to defend,” he said.

articles.title: Nike’s Air Max 1000 are almost entirely 3D-printed
articles.summary: Nike’s new Air Max 1000 are the company’s first 3D-printed shoes made from a single lightweight flexible material.
articles.body_text: Nike’s new Air Max 1000 are the company’s first shoes manufactured almost entirely using 3D printing. Debuting at ComplexCon this past weekend in Las Vegas, Nike collaborated with Zellerfeld — a company that already has expertise in 3D printing shoes — to create the Air Max 1000, but they’re not currently available to the general public. The Air Max 1000’s design is an updated take on the Air Max 1, which debuted in 1987 as Nike’s first shoe with an air cushion in the heel that was visible through a window in the midsole. That feature is carried forward to the new Air Max 1000, and although the air cushion itself isn’t 3D-printed, the rest of the shoe uses a single flexible material. [Image: Everything except the Air Max 1000’s air cushion is 3D-printed. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25739581/nikeairmax2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] By mixing layers with varying densities and textures, the outsole on the bottom of the Air Max 1000 remains firm and supportive, while the upper parts of the shoe are more flexible and comfortable, allowing them to be slipped on and off without the need for laces. [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l4qXAeMAWUI] The use of 3D printing also allowed Nike to realize the Air Max 1000’s unique contoured design, which the company says would have been impossible using traditional shoe manufacturing techniques. “As an innovator, what’s most exciting to me about the Air Max 1000 are the new solutions we can achieve with next-level manufacturing,” says John Hoke, Nike’s Chief Innovation Officer. Nike originally announced the Air Max 1000 in a solid bright red colorway, but influencers at the event later revealed additional colors of the shoe, including orange, white, blue, and black with a green air cushion. And while Nike distributed a small number of pairs of the Air Max 1000 at the event, wider availability was limited to 1,000 pairs that attendees could win the chance to preorder, according to Elliot Page, who also shared a brief video review of the shoes. Nike hasn’t revealed plans for a wider general release of the Air Max 1000, nor has it revealed what the pricing might be. But the 3D-printed shoes now available on Zellerfeld’s website range in price from $159 for a sandal design to almost $400 for a high-top. The Air Max 1000 aren’t the first time Nike has used 3D printing to make shoes. In 2017, the company debuted its VaporFly Elite Flyprint with a lighter and more breathable fabric material it claimed was the “first 3D-printed textile upper in performance footwear.” Other companies, such as Adidas, already sell shoes with 3D-printed midsoles. But like Nike, Adidas is also experimenting with shoes made entirely from 3D-printed materials, including its new Climacool24 that debuted in October.

articles.title: Waste in space: all the news surrounding space junk
articles.summary: The latest news about space junk and global cleanup efforts.
articles.body_text: What goes up, must come down — unless you’re sending things into space, of course, which creates some complications. After more than 60 years of satellite launches and space exploration, manufactured objects like derelict spacecraft and rocket fragments now litter Earth’s orbit as space junk. The waste has damaged or even outright destroyed active spacecraft it collides with and even caused property damage down here on terra firma when debris has failed to burn up in the atmosphere. Some efforts, from net-casting satellites to “Zero Debris” space sustainability initiatives, have been made to address the growing problem. But with analysts estimating that over 2,800 satellites will be launched each year between now and 2032, more needs to be done to ensure that the space around Earth is safe. We’re collecting our coverage about space junk here to keep you updated.

Samtal har förts hela veckan och källor beskriver att man har kommit en bit på vägen, även om inget är klart än. Och Nooshi Dadgostars regeringskrav står fast. Tillsammans med Centerns inställning om att vägra sitta i en regering ihop med Västerpartiet har det hittills satt krokben för Anderssons rödgröna regeringsplaner. Nu kan S-ledaren stå inför ytterligare ett hinder. Källor i C beskriver en plan som återigen ska bana väg för ett centerpartistiskt sidbyte. Personer som vill se Ulf Kristersson som statsminister uppges trycka på för att Andersson ska prövas i den tredje statsministeromröstningen. De räknar med att hon då röstas ner av Vänsterpartiet eftersom regeringskravet inte är utlöst, och att Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist då, inför hotet om ett extraval, ska landa i att det är bättre att C väljer Ulf Kristersson. Själv har C-ledaren inte uteslutit extraval som ett möjligt utfall.
